skill.work: We have a huge backlog after the holidays.
skill.everyday: The new mall near our house is massive.
skill.analogy: 'Very big' is a plain roti; 'huge' is the one that puffs up.
skill.insteadOf: We have a very big backlog after the holidays.

skill.work: It's a tiny change; it'll take ten minutes.
skill.everyday: Our first flat had a tiny kitchen.
skill.analogy: 'Tiny' is a single cardamom pod: you picture it at once.
skill.insteadOf: It's a very small change.

skill.work: The meeting room AC is freezing; can we turn it up?
skill.everyday: Delhi mornings in January are freezing.
skill.analogy: 'Freezing' makes them reach for a shawl; 'very cold' just reports the weather.
skill.insteadOf: The meeting room AC is very cold.

skill.work: The office was boiling when the AC broke.
skill.everyday: It's scorching in Chennai in May.
skill.analogy: 'Boiling' is the pressure cooker whistle; 'very hot' is just a warm pan.
skill.insteadOf: The office was very hot when the AC broke.

skill.work: I'm delighted to welcome Fatima to the team.
skill.everyday: Mum was thrilled with her birthday surprise.
skill.analogy: 'Thrilled' is a last-ball six; 'very happy' is a quiet single.
skill.insteadOf: I'm very happy to welcome Fatima to the team.

skill.work: I felt miserable after the demo crashed.
skill.everyday: My son was heartbroken when India lost the final.
skill.analogy: 'Very sad' is a grey sky; 'miserable' is the rain soaking you.
skill.insteadOf: I felt very sad after the demo crashed.

skill.work: I was terrified before my first client presentation.
skill.everyday: My niece is petrified of lizards.
skill.analogy: 'Terrified' is the horror film's loud music; 'very scared' is only the trailer.
skill.insteadOf: I was very scared before my first client presentation.

skill.work: I was stunned when they approved the plan in one meeting.
skill.everyday: I was amazed the auto driver had change for 500.
skill.analogy: 'Stunned' is the batter frozen as the stumps fly; 'very surprised' is a raised eyebrow.
skill.insteadOf: I was very surprised when they approved the plan.

skill.work: Testing is crucial before Friday's release.
skill.everyday: Sleep is vital the night before an exam.
skill.analogy: 'Crucial' is the last over of the match: everything turns on it.
skill.insteadOf: Testing is very important before Friday's release.

skill.work: It was a gruelling week of back-to-back client calls.
skill.everyday: The trek to Kedarnath is gruelling but worth it.
skill.analogy: 'Gruelling' is the hill climb you feel in your legs the next day.
skill.insteadOf: It was a very difficult week of client calls.

skill.work: The new tool makes deploys straightforward.
skill.everyday: UPI makes paying the milkman effortless.
skill.analogy: 'Effortless' is a downhill cycle ride: you don't even pedal.
skill.insteadOf: The new tool makes deploys very easy.

skill.work: The vendor's quote is steep for a three-week job.
skill.everyday: Airport taxis are steep after midnight.
skill.analogy: Like a steep ghat road: the price climbs fast and you feel it.
skill.insteadOf: The vendor's quote is very expensive for a three-week job.

skill.work: This laptop is ancient; it takes five minutes to start.
skill.everyday: We found an antique clock at the Sunday market.
skill.analogy: 'Ancient' brings temple ruins to mind; 'very old' could mean last year.
skill.insteadOf: This laptop is very old.

skill.work: The new pantry is spotless; let's keep it that way.
skill.everyday: Mum keeps the kitchen spotless before Diwali.
skill.analogy: 'Spotless' means not one spot, like a freshly washed white kurta.
skill.insteadOf: The new pantry is very clean.

skill.work: The meeting room whiteboard is filthy; can we get it cleaned?
skill.everyday: The kids came home filthy after cricket in the rain.
skill.analogy: 'Filthy' is a kurta after Holi; 'very dirty' is just one stain.
skill.insteadOf: The meeting room whiteboard is very dirty.

skill.work: The afternoon sun is glaring on my screen.
skill.everyday: The Diwali lights on our street were dazzling.
skill.analogy: 'Dazzling' makes you squint, like headlights on a highway at night.
skill.insteadOf: The afternoon sun is very bright on my screen.

skill.work: The drilling next door is deafening; let's move the call.
skill.everyday: The wedding band was deafening, but everyone danced.
skill.analogy: 'Deafening' is a baraat drum right next to your ear.
skill.insteadOf: The drilling next door is very loud.

skill.work: The floor went silent after the announcement.
skill.everyday: A hushed crowd waited for the result.
skill.analogy: 'Silent' is the stadium the moment the star batter is out.
skill.insteadOf: The floor became very quiet after the announcement.

skill.work: The team made rapid progress this sprint.
skill.everyday: We took a brisk walk around the lake after dinner.
skill.analogy: 'Brisk' is the morning walker who overtakes you in the park.
skill.insteadOf: The team made very fast progress this sprint.

skill.work: The test server is sluggish today; deploys take ten minutes.
skill.everyday: Traffic on Outer Ring Road moved at a glacial pace.
skill.analogy: 'Sluggish' is a Monday-morning auto that won't start first time.
skill.insteadOf: The test server is very slow today.

skill.work: Her talk on user research was fascinating.
skill.everyday: The new web series is gripping; I watched four episodes.
skill.analogy: 'Gripping' is a thriller that holds your collar till the last scene.
skill.insteadOf: Her talk on user research was very interesting.

skill.work: The two-hour compliance training was tedious.
skill.everyday: The train ride was dull without my phone.
skill.analogy: 'Tedious' is counting the same stack of forms twice.
skill.insteadOf: The two-hour compliance training was very boring.

skill.work: Rahul's farewell speech was hilarious.
skill.everyday: Dad's face when the cake slid off the plate was priceless.
skill.analogy: 'Hilarious' is laughing so hard you spill your chai.
skill.insteadOf: Rahul's farewell speech was very funny.

skill.work: The outage report looks grim: logins failed for an hour.
skill.everyday: The doctor looked grave, but Nani's tests came back fine.
skill.analogy: 'Grim' is dark clouds over the stadium before the final.
skill.insteadOf: The outage report looks very serious.

skill.work: The cafeteria is packed at one; let's eat at noon.
skill.everyday: The Diwali market was packed.
skill.analogy: 'Packed' is a Mumbai local at 9 a.m.: not one more person fits.
skill.insteadOf: The cafeteria is very crowded at one.

skill.work: The office is deserted on Friday evenings.
skill.everyday: The beach was deserted at 6 a.m.
skill.analogy: 'Deserted' is a railway platform after the last train has gone.
skill.insteadOf: The office is very empty on Friday evenings.

skill.work: I got soaked walking from the parking lot.
skill.everyday: The kids came back drenched from the rain.
skill.analogy: 'Drenched' is a monsoon downpour, not a light drizzle.
skill.insteadOf: I got very wet walking from the parking lot.

skill.work: After the two-hour workshop, everyone was parched.
skill.everyday: I was parched after the cricket match in the sun.
skill.analogy: 'Parched' is dry fields in May, waiting for the first rain.
skill.insteadOf: Everyone was very thirsty after the workshop.

skill.work: Riya's fix was brilliant; it halved the load time.
skill.everyday: My nephew is sharp; he solved the puzzle in a minute.
skill.analogy: 'Sharp' is a fresh kitchen knife: it cuts through a problem fast.
skill.insteadOf: Riya's fix was very smart.

skill.work: Our first buyers are affluent families in Pune.
skill.everyday: Her uncle is well-off; he owns three shops.
skill.analogy: 'Well-off' says it quietly, like a nod; 'very rich' says it on a loudspeaker.
skill.insteadOf: Our first buyers are very rich families in Pune.

skill.work: It's a powerful tool once you learn the shortcuts.
skill.everyday: This table is sturdy enough to stand on.
skill.analogy: 'Sturdy' is a steel almirah: it won't wobble.
skill.insteadOf: It's a very strong tool once you learn the shortcuts.

skill.work: Without user data, our argument looks feeble.
skill.everyday: My grandmother is frail now, so we visit every Sunday.
skill.analogy: 'Feeble' is a phone torch trying to light a whole hall.
skill.insteadOf: Without user data, our argument looks very weak.

skill.work: The new dashboard design is stunning.
skill.everyday: The view from Nandi Hills at sunrise was stunning.
skill.analogy: 'Stunning' stops you mid-step, like your first sight of the Taj.
skill.insteadOf: The new dashboard design is very beautiful.

skill.work: The old login page looks hideous on mobile.
skill.everyday: The new flyover is an unsightly block of concrete.
skill.analogy: 'Unsightly' is a pile of rubble blocking a lovely view.
skill.insteadOf: The old login page looks very ugly on mobile.

skill.work: Arjun is meticulous; he checks every number twice.
skill.everyday: My dad is meticulous about his car's service dates.
skill.analogy: 'Meticulous' is a tailor measuring twice before one cut.
skill.insteadOf: Arjun is very careful; he checks every number twice.

skill.work: I'm certain the fix is live; I tested it myself.
skill.everyday: I'm positive I left my keys on the table.
skill.analogy: 'Certain' is a stamped receipt; 'very sure' is only a promise.
skill.insteadOf: I'm very sure the fix is live.

skill.work: The client sounded anxious about the launch date.
skill.everyday: I felt uneasy when Mum didn't pick up the phone.
skill.analogy: 'Uneasy' is the knot in your stomach while the exam result loads.
skill.insteadOf: The client sounded very worried about the launch date.

skill.work: The release had numerous small issues; let's list them.
skill.everyday: We had endless trouble with the new washing machine.
skill.analogy: 'Countless' is stars on a village night: you give up counting.
skill.insteadOf: The release had a lot of problems.

skill.work: Thanks, that was a lovely send-off for Fatima.
skill.everyday: We had a lovely dinner at my aunt's place.
skill.analogy: 'Lovely' is a warm smile; 'really nice' is a polite nod.
skill.insteadOf: That was a really nice send-off for Fatima.

skill.work: My first draft was awful; this one is much better.
skill.everyday: Traffic on Sunday was dreadful; we sat for an hour.
skill.analogy: 'Dreadful' is a three-hour jam on the Mumbai-Pune expressway.
skill.insteadOf: My first draft was really bad.
